I4.quote: Norit Darco activated carbon (G-60) was also examined. Although this wood based carbon generally has a surface area only around 700 m2/g with a relatively low mesopore volume
I4.location: PDF p. 2 (journal p. 2292), Section 2.1.1 Conventional carbons

notes: I4 is borderline and is the only criterion in doubt. The ~700 m2/g is a typical value for the commercial Norit Darco G-60 grade ('generally has ... around'), not an area measured in this work; no method or probe gas is stated (schema: surface_area_method = unspecified, area_same_sample = unclear). G-60 is a measured sample (Table 1, PCI 0.041±0.014 wt.% at 23°C, 3.59 MPa), and I4 accepts any method, so I coded it met. No other sample has a numerical area: VGCF is described only as having an area ~70 times smaller, citing [10]. If the resolver reads I4 as requiring an area measured or reported specifically for the tested specimen, the code becomes no_surface_area. Other observations: all carbon uptakes are at room temperature (23°C; Fig. 14 at 25°C); the high-pressure manual system values (<0.7, <0.5, <0.2 wt.% at 11 MPa) are stated upper limits; PCI values are near background ('not significantly above the background'). Metal hydrides (LaNi5, Nd2Fe14B) are calibration standards, not carbon sorbents. Text layer renders the degree sign as '8' throughout; Table 1 checked against the page image.
